claims_checked.claim: Scrum definition: lightweight framework ... adaptive solutions for complex problems
Shorter Sprints generate more learning cycles and limit risk of cost and effort to a smaller time frame
Sprints enable predictability by inspection and adaptation toward a Product Goal at least every calendar month
Quality does not decrease during the Sprint
Scrum makes visible the relative efficacy of current management, environment and work techniques
Scrum is purposefully incomplete
Multiple Increments may be created within a Sprint; Sprint Review is not a gate to releasing value
Those wanting to change the Product Backlog must convince the Product Owner
Implementing only parts of Scrum is possible, but the result is not Scrum
Scrum Team typically 10 or fewer people
'The Guide describes a single team' (limitations table)
claims_checked.source: https://scrumguides.org/scrum-guide.html (Guide advises reorganising into multiple cohesive Scrum Teams sharing Product Goal, Product Backlog and Product Owner)

claims_checked.claim: One-month maximum timeboxes 8h/4h/3h, Daily Scrum 15 min; halving for two-week Sprints labelled common practice
2017 Guide: refinement usually consumes no more than 10% of Development Team capacity; removed in 2020

Effectiveness = stakeholder satisfaction and team morale; five factors
Stakeholder concern largest direct effect (beta .513), responsiveness significant direct effect (beta .402)
Management support works only indirectly; 'management support in itself will not make teams more effective'
Limitations: cross-sectional, team-member-rated outcomes, voluntary sample, software teams
'Most articles on Scrum's advantages cite no evidence'
'Many teams report higher ownership as a result'

changes_made: Removed unsupported generalisation 'Most articles on Scrum's advantages cite no evidence'; research section now opens 'Claims about Scrum's benefits are easier to make than to test.'
Advantage 7: replaced unsourced 'Many teams report higher ownership as a result' with a pointer to team autonomy as one of the five factors in the Verwijs and Russo study.

Worked example scenario changed from 'a customer self-service portal' to 'an online appointment-booking system for a chain of dental clinics' to avoid echoing the 7-person self-service-portal example on /project-management/scrum/increment-in-scrum/ (figures unchanged).

Limitations table, 'Coordination across many teams': 'The Guide describes a single team' corrected to state that beyond sharing one Product Goal, Product Backlog and Product Owner, the Guide says little about coordinating teams.

unresolved_issues: Duplication check: similarity 0.679 with /project-management/scrum/what-is-scrum/ is shared Scrum vocabulary. Intent differs: what-is-scrum explains the framework and has a six-row benefits/limitations summary ending 'Read next Advantages of Scrum'; this page covers mechanism, preconditions, evidence, cost and a fit checklist. Its 'When Scrum's advantages outweigh its costs' table overlaps in theme with what-is-scrum's 'When to use Scrum' table but is framed by lost advantages, not situations. No reused examples found.
'Zombie Scrum' is presented as an informal term without a citation (acceptable as 'sometimes called').
